messages:
mike-infra: heads-up — at ~02:10 UTC eu2 started dropping a subset of gpu pods in the edge slice. noticed pod restarts + scheduler evictions :warning:

claire-sre: seeing the same in kube metrics — node churn + queueing spike for realtime prefixes. latency SLOs tripped briefly.

incident-bot: Incident opened: INC-2026-2384 1: region eu2 degraded (auto-detected pod_eviction_rate > 3/min)

mike-infra: we kicked a soft divert to warm pools in us-west to reduce user impact. did a staged ramp to avoid hot-shots.

ben-platform: saw cross-region egress and burst gpu allocation on billing — rough delta +28% for the hour. logging to cost channel.

alice-cost: can you paste exact weights and the command you ran so i can run cost sim?

mike-infra: weights + command:
```
redwood-shift --from eu2 --to us-west --strategy staged --steps "30,50,70" --step-interval 120s
```
start: eu2 70% / us-west 30% -> ramped to eu2 30% / us-west 70% over ~6m.

claire-sre: root cause appears to be cni interface flaps + kubelet oom churn on older gpu node images. isolating old-ami nodes and cordoning.

ben-platform: action: add a pre-shift validation in the runbook to check node image drift + cni health before starting staged diversions. avoid shifting into a region with known drift.

mike-infra: also enforce ramp caps: max per-step delta 20% and min step interval 2m unless manual override. prevents sudden routing jumps and hoarding of kv-cache.

alice-cost: add a cost-forecast step: estimate cross-region egress + burst gpu needs. if projected cost > 15% of hourly baseline require finance-oncall approval.

claire-sre: proposed alert thresholds to add to runbook and alerts:
- if cni_flap_rate > 2/min AND pod_eviction_rate > 1/min -> page infra-oncall
- sustained queueing latency > 300ms for 5m -> automated soft-divert to warm-pools
- reserve_capacity < 1.2x peak -> block >50% of routes shifting to target region

mike-infra: rollback policy: if downstream 5xxs or increased error-rate after a step, roll back that step by 50% within 3m and escalate to product-owner channel. make the automation highlight rollback candidates.

ben-platform: adding automation guard: prevent shifting more than N concurrent routes if target reserve < 1.2x expected peak. will add unit test + simulated failure mode.

claire-sre: TODOs for runbook PR: pre-shift checks (node-image, cni health, reserve), ramp caps, cost-forecast + approval gate, rollback policy, owners for each step, and a post-shift validation checklist. i'll open the PR today and link it here.

alice-cost: assigned: @claire-sre update runbook; @ben-platform change automation; @mike-infra draft postmortem + capacity recommendation; @alice-cost prepare cost impact report and drill plan.

mike-infra: operational note: we cordoned 6 nodes and reimaged 4. churn subsided ~02:48 UTC. warm-pool diversion kept user-visible errors low.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-2384 resolved at 02:50 UTC. summary and actions captured.

claire-sre: will run a short retro tomorrow + paste the runbook PR here. also propose a scheduled drill (quarterly) to exercise staged diversion and cost-approval path. :heavy_check_mark:

ben-platform: adding the drill to Q2 ops calendar and tagging infra-automation for a dry-run.

alice-cost: once runbook merges, i'll run cost sims for typical traffic profiles and set alarm thresholds. we should also set an automated dry-run that simulates cost projection without actually diverting traffic.

mike-infra: thanks everyone. closing notes: add a small blameless postmortem paragraph to the doc (AMI drift + CNI regressions), recommend a proactive reimage cadence for older GPU AMIs, and add a preflight script to the shift tooling.

claire-sre: agreed. PR link will be posted here when ready.
